messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — spotted an unexpected invoice adjustment labeled 'REGIONAL_RECLASS_RECONCILE' for us-west1 GPU hours, ~USD 13,450. Anyone else?
Elaine: I pulled the billing CSV and see matching accelerator usage lines + separate reconcilation addon lines. Saving a snippet below.
Samir: Did we change any commitments or resize pools in Feb? I didn't push any changes.
Jordan: No changes on our side — commitments still active for the usual pools.
billing-bot: billing-alert: Retroactive adjustment > $1k detected on project:redwood-inference-prod for invoice 2026-03. Reference INV-2026-03-4890
Elaine: CSV excerpt:
```
line_item_id,service,sku,usage_start,usage_end,amount
LI-90210,Compute Engine,ACCELERATOR_NVIDIA_A100_US_WEST1,2026-02-12T00:00:00Z,2026-02-12T01:00:00Z,6725.00
LI-90211,Compute Engine,REGIONAL_RECLASS_RECONCILE,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,2026-02-28T23:59:59Z,6725.00
```
Elaine: amounts are mirrored and windows overlap; looks like they backfilled a new addon SKU instead of swapping.
Natalie: I'm on it — pinged the cloud vendor account team to confirm if there was a SKU taxonomy change.
Chris: We had a few burst jobs on preemptible nodes last week — could transient autoscaling trigger a weird classification?
Jordan: The disputed lines indicate sustained (non-preempt) accelerator usage in their metadata, so unlikely tied to transient preemptible runs.
Samir: Can you grab the full set of affected line_item_ids and project tags? I'll map to committed pools.
Elaine: Uploading full CSV to the finance folder. Items mostly tag to rwd-prod-gpu-1 and rwd-batch-2 pools.
billing-bot: note: historical records show SKU split event on vendor side: ACCELERATOR_NVIDIA_A100 -> ACCELERATOR_NVIDIA_A100 + REGIONAL_RECLASS_ADDON on 2026-02-25
Natalie: Vendor confirmed a taxonomy update and an automated backfill that was supposed to add credits AND reclassify, but they now say the credit step failed for some projects.
Chris: So they effectively duplicated charges by adding a new addon line without offsetting credit. That's... not great.
Elaine: I opened ticket VND-9034. Requested an immediate temporary credit and a forensic of which automation step failed.
Jordan: Finance impact: if not remediated quickly, this will push us over our committed GPU spend target for US-WEST and impact forecast.
Samir: I'll run a quick delta analysis by committed pool and submit to accounting. ETA 4 hours.
Natalie: Vendor provided an interim credit hold: HOLD-CR-5612 for -$13,450 pending settlement. They expect resolution within 48–72 hours.
Elaine: Accounting asked for a one-page incident memo. I'll draft: include CSV sample, vendor ticket link, projected cashflow wobble.
Chris: Operational action item: add SKU-change webhook to cloud-account notifications and create a billing reconciliation gate so we don't auto-approve any vendor reclassifications.
Jordan: Agree. Add to infra-billing-ops backlog and tag it P0 for alerts on taxonomy changes.
Samir: After the credit posts, I'll reconcile committed discounts to make sure our committed GPU credits still apply correctly to net usage.
Elaine: Vendor updated ticket: root cause was a failing lambda that applied offset credits conditionally; error handling suppressed failures. They're rolling a fix.
billing-bot: update: HOLD-CR-5612 moved to APPLIED on 2026-03-18T16:20:03Z
Elaine: Credit applied; invoice recalculated. Finance says the net change is zero after the credit; closing vendor ticket after they provide postmortem.
Jordan: Confirmed final numbers against committed pool metadata — all matched. Thanks for the fast turnaround.
Chris: I'll draft the alert rule and a short playbook for handling vendor-led SKU reorganizations.
Elaine: Closing thread. Final ask to vendor in postmortem: include timeline, root-cause of credit-step failure, and measures to prevent future silent failures. :white_check_mark:
